cohort: Newborns aged <28 days admitted to the NICU of a teaching hospital in Eastern India, excluding those with major congenital anomalies, born outside the hospital, or without parental consent.
finding: The study found a 16.28% prevalence of hypocalcemia in the NICU, predominantly affecting males and newborns with a birth weight >=2500g.
mod_finding: Lower Uterine Caesarean Section (LUCS) was the most common mode of delivery (78.58%) among newborns with hypocalcemia.
